title: Classroom Management And The Power Of Your Personality your-personality/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin pushes back on the notion that teachers need to suppress their personality to manage a classroom effectively, arguing instead that authentic charisma makes classroom management easier. He offers seven concrete suggestions for showing more personality: being oneself, loosening up, standing tall and confident, staying fully present, focusing on the rewards of working with students, joining in student activities, and closing emotional distance rather than taking misbehavior personally. He closes with an anecdote about visiting a relaxed, joyful third-grade classroom, concluding that the teacher's secret was a combination of an uncompromising classroom management plan, deep belief in her students, and letting her personality shine through.
points: Suppressing personality to appear stricter is counterproductive; authentic charisma and likability make classroom management easier, not harder.
A classroom is described as an ideal place to be more authentically oneself, free from generational social constraints.
Joining students in recess games or activities is offered as a simple, direct way to build rapport and show personality.
Not taking misbehavior personally is framed as a way to close, rather than widen, emotional distance between teacher and students.
The strongest classrooms combine an uncompromising management plan, deep belief in students, and a teacher's personality shining through.
quotes: In fact, sharing your uniqueness, your charisma, and your joie de vivre with your students makes classroom management easier, not harder.
It’s your personality that draws students in, makes you worth listening to, and gives them a compelling reason to want to behave.

A classroom is the perfect place to be more you than just about anywhere else. Because of the stark difference in generations, you’re free to throw off the social constraints of your age, peers, and professional acquaintances.

We talk a lot on this website about not taking misbehavior personally, about how it undermines classroom management. But it also creates distance between you and your students. Your personality, on the other hand, is what draws them closer and endears you to them.
She is uncompromising with her classroom management plan. Her belief in her students, both behaviorally and academically, is off the charts. And her personality shines into every corner of the room.
